pedagogical_level: undergraduate fundamentals course with hands-on Java practice
course_intent: Teach the foundations of object-oriented programming using Java — students should leave able to write Java programs using classes, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, and interfaces, and to apply core OOP design principles.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the level of core Java syntax, OOP language mechanics, and introductory class design with hands-on coding. Advanced Java topics (generics internals, concurrency, JVM internals, design patterns at depth, frameworks like Spring, JavaFX/GUI, file I/O, networking, lambdas/streams) and formal type-theory of OOP are beyond this course's depth bound.
key_topics: Java syntax basics (variables, data types, operators, type casting)
Control flow (if/else, switch, while/do-while/for loops, break/continue)
Methods, parameter passing, overloading, and variable scope
Classes, objects, constructors, and UML class diagrams
Wrapper classes, String/StringBuilder, BigInteger/BigDecimal, regex basics
Inheritance with super keyword and constructor chaining
Polymorphism, dynamic binding, instanceof, and ArrayList
one_liner: Introductory object-oriented programming in Java covering syntax, control flow, methods, arrays, classes, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstract classes/interfaces — does NOT cover generics in depth, lambdas/streams, concurrency, GUI, file I/O, networking, design patterns, or frameworks.
